question: A hospital implements pharmacogenomic clinical decision support that only fires an alert when a clinician attempts to prescribe a drug. Alert override rates are 75%. Which strategy is most likely to improve appropriate PGx utilization?
explanation: Evidence from the IGNITE network shows that proactive (pre-emptive) display of PGx results in patient summary views — before the prescribing decision is made — dramatically improves appropriate utilization compared to reactive alerts at prescription time. Reactive alerts are often dismissed as interruptions; proactive display integrates genomic information into the natural clinical reasoning process.
